$schema-note: Hand-maintained. Data, not code: nothing under src/ imports this file.
purpose: The guard ledger for WIN-258 TRANCHE 5 — `channels`' canonical store, the
SIXTH context owner behind the one PostgreSQL client ADR M0.3 §15 gives the
ORM. One entry per guard: per scope predicate, per vocabulary the schema does
not carry, per column a database rule refuses to move, per boundary the claim
predicate and the lease fence must agree on, and per statement the port's
contract says must be one statement. Each carries the file it lives in, the
EXACT text that implements it (`from`), the edit that removes it (`to`), and
the NAMED cases that were seen to go red (`kills`).
IT IS A SIXTH FILE beside mutations.json, mutations-identity.json,
mutations-ports.json, mutations-outbox.json, mutations-tools.json,
mutations-agents.json and mutations-cost.json rather than an extension of any
of them, for the reason the others are separate: each tranche is a separate
claim about a separate port surface, and a reader checking one should not have
to read past the rest. All of them are hashed by the same
packages.adapters.config rule and counted together by the v1 ledger.
WHY THIS TRANCHE NEEDED ITS OWN SWEEP. Three of the six rows are written on
the INBOUND path — the inbox, the thread link, the installation's
`lastEventAt` — which runs before anything else in the system can, at
at-least-once delivery, with several workers on one table. Its hardest
promises are all about what does NOT happen: an admitted payload that cannot
be moved, a lease that expires exactly now and is still held, an availability
that has elapsed exactly now and is claimable, and a conflicting link that
must name the thread that won. None of those is visible in a returned value
on a store with one caller, which is exactly the shape of guard a green suite
hides.
procedure: PROVE THE SUITES GREEN FIRST. Tranche 1's first sweep reported 22 kills and
every one was VACUOUS: a context's `dist` had been cleaned, so every suite
failed to load its import and would have 'died' against any mutation at all,
including none. The driver runs each suite set UNMUTATED and refuses to sweep
unless it is green with a non-zero executed case count, and classifies a run
with no executed cases as VACUOUS rather than as a kill.
EVERY ENTRY NAMES THE WHOLE SUITE SET, AND THAT IS TRANCHE 5's LESSON RATHER
THAN CAUTION. `cost-monitoring`'s second sweep scored six of its forty entries
with zero executed cases: each edit compiled and collected, then broke the
conformance suite while it was BUILDING its transcript, in a `beforeAll`, so
vitest reported every case in that file SKIPPED and no named case went red. A
suite set that turns red only through a setup crash names no promise. This
ledger was written with the wide set from the start, and the same failure was
observed once here for real: a harness collision on
`AgentVersion(agentId, versionNumber)` skipped all ten cases of the rules
suite and the run reported nothing failing.
THE SUITES ARE FIVE INTEGRATION FILES AND ONE PURE ONE. The pure file is the
only one `pnpm test:v1-packages` runs; the other five need a real PostgreSQL
and run in the `postgres-tenancy-repository` CI job, which FAILS rather than
skips when Docker is absent.
THE FIRST SWEEP SCORED 47 KILLED AND ONE SURVIVOR, AND THE SURVIVOR IS WHY
THE SCENARIO HAS THIRTY-SIX OBSERVATIONS RATHER THAN THIRTY-FIVE. M-L03
labels every link read through `findThreadLink` as a `connection` link, and
the whole set stayed green: every single-link read in the scenario used a
CONNECTION owner, so reading `ChannelAppThread` and then mislabelling the row
was invisible. `findThreadLink(installation)` is the observation that closes
it — the same key, read back through the other half of the union — and it was
added to the shared scenario rather than to a suite of its own precisely
because the in-memory double answers it too, so the two transcripts compare
on it. Re-run alone, M-L03 is KILLED by
`their transcripts match, observation for observation`.
FINAL: 48 entries, 48 KILLED by a NAMED case, 0 SURVIVED, 0 VACUOUS, 0 STALE,
0 KILLED-UNNAMED. The baseline ran 72 executed cases green before any mutation
was applied, and the mutated runs executed 72 as well — no run scored a kill
through a collection failure or a crashed hook.

mutations.name: M-N01 connections: the environment filter that hides another tenant's row

mutations.note: A row is persisted under an organization that does not own it. `enforce_domain_ancestry` checks the environment and the three references and NONE of the two parents the value claims.
kills: an environment that does not exist is a different refusal from one that is not yours

mutations.name: M-N04 connections: the unknown-environment refusal, distinct from the forged one
mutations.note: Two different mistakes collapse into one answer: an environment that never existed and one that is not yours become indistinguishable in a log.

mutations.note: `"Slack"` is stored beside `"slack"`. The column is plain TEXT, so this guard is the only thing between an operator's capitalisation and a connection its own adapter registry can never find.

mutations.name: M-B06 inbox: the claim order that stops a row being starved
mutations.from: const CLAIM_ORDER = [{ availableAt: "asc" }, { createdAt: "asc" }] as const;
mutations.to: const CLAIM_ORDER = [{ availableAt: "desc" }, { createdAt: "asc" }] as const;
mutations.note: The newest events are served first, so the oldest waiting row is starved for as long as new deliveries keep arriving.
